request.input:
Bill number: HB1163
<bill_text>
SENATE BILL 1019
 By White

 HOUSE BILL 1163

 By Stevens

 AN ACT to amend Chapter __ of the Public Acts of 2025
 (1st Ex. Sess. – SB 6001 / HB 6004); and
 Tennessee Code Annotated, Title 49, Chapter 13
 and Title 49, Chapter 3, relative to education
 funding for public charter schools.

BE IT ENACTED BY THE GENERAL ASSEMBLY OF THE STATE OF TENNESSEE:

 SECTION 1. Tennessee Code Annotated, Section 49-3-103(d)(3), is amended by

adding the language "or public charter school" after the language "Explain how an LEA".

 SECTION 2. Tennessee Code Annotated, Section 49-3-105, is amended by deleting

subsection (d) and substituting instead the following:

 (d)

 (1) The funding that a student generates pursuant to this section must be

 administered and allocated by the department to the LEA in which the student is

 a member for the duration of the student's membership in the LEA, except that:

 (A) The funding a student generates pursuant to subdivision

 (c)(3) must not be allocated to the LEA, but must be maintained by the

 department; and

 (B) The state share of the funding a public charter school student

 generates for an LEA pursuant to this section must not be allocated to the

 LEA, but must be allocated directly to the public charter school.

 (2) A student's membership in an LEA begins on the first day of the

 student's membership and ends on the last day of the student's membership in

 the LEA, except that the membership of a student who graduates early is

 extended to the student's expected graduation date for funding purposes.

 SECTION 3. Tennessee Code Annotated, Section 49-3-316, is amended by adding the

language "or public charter school" after the language "LEA" wherever it appears in subsection

(c) and by adding the following as a new subsection:

 (f)

 (1) The commissioner, in consultation with the comptroller of the

 treasury, shall develop, revise as necessary, and prescribe a standardized

 system of financial accounting and reporting for all public charter schools,

 including appropriate forms or other documentation. This system must be

 designed to facilitate year-to-year and agency-to-agency comparison, as well as

 adequately indicating the sources and uses of all funds received by each public

 charter school. The commissioner shall review the fiscal public school records in

 all public charter schools to the end that the expenditure of funds, whether for

 current operation and maintenance purposes, capital outlay purposes, and other

 school purposes, are properly accounted for and safeguarded.

 (2) The commissioner may require public charter schools that receive

 allocations of state education funding pursuant to part 1 of this chapter or

 otherwise to comply with one (1) or more of the requirements established for

 LEAs in this section, as the commissioner deems appropriate or applicable.

 SECTION 4. Tennessee Code Annotated, Section 49-13-112, is amended by deleting

subsection (a) and substituting instead the following:

 (a)

 (1) A local board of education shall allocate to the public charter school

 an amount equal to:

 (A) The local student-generated funds for member students in the

 public charter school for the prior year in alignment with the TISA

 pursuant to chapter 3, part 1 of this title;

 (B) The average per pupil state and local funds received by the

 district in the current school year above those required by the TISA for

 each member student in the public charter school in the prior year;

 (C) The per student state and local funds received by the LEA for

 member students in the public charter school in the current school year

 beyond the prior year's membership; and

 (D) All appropriate allocations under federal law or regulation,

 including, but not limited to, IDEA and ESEA funds.

 (2) The department of education shall allocate directly to the public

charter school an amount equal to the state student-generated funds for member

students in the public charter school for the prior year in alignment with the TISA

pursuant to chapter 3, part 1 of this title.

 (3) Federal funds received by the LEA must be disbursed to public

charter schools authorized by the LEA by either joint agreement on shared

services by individual public charter schools or sub-grants to a public charter

school for the public charter school's equitable share of the federal grant based

on eligible students. The allocation must be made in accordance with the

policies and procedures developed by the department of education.

 (4) Each LEA shall include as part of its budget submitted pursuant to §

49-2-203, the per pupil amount of local money it will pass through to public

charter schools during the upcoming school year, including all calculations listed

in this section. Allocations to public charter schools during that year must be

 based on the calculated amounts. The LEA shall distribute the portion of local

 funds it expects to receive in no fewer than nine (9) equal installments to public

 charter schools in the same manner as state funds are distributed pursuant to

 chapter 3 of this title. An LEA shall adjust local payments to public charter

 schools, at a minimum, in October, February, and June, based on changes in

 revenue, student membership, or student services. All funds received by a public

 charter school must be spent according to the budget submitted or as otherwise

 revised by the public charter school governing body, subject to the requirements

 of state and federal law.

 SECTION 5. Sections 1 and 3 of this act take effect upon becoming a law, the public

welfare requiring it. For rulemaking purposes, Sections 2 and 4 of this act take effect upon

becoming a law, the public welfare requiring it. For all other purposes, Sections 2 and 4 of this

act take effect July 1, 2025, the public welfare requiring it.
</bill_text>

<summary>
This bill would change how public charter schools are funded and tracked under Tennessee's education funding law, which the text refers to as the TISA. It would send the state share of funding for charter school students directly to the charter school instead of to the local school system (LEA).

Section 1 would add "or public charter school" to a provision in Section 49-3-103(d)(3) that begins "Explain how an LEA." The text does not show what the provision requires.

Section 2 would replace Section 49-3-105(d). Funding a student generates would go through the state department of education to the LEA where the student is a member, for as long as the student is a member. There are two exceptions. Funding generated under subdivision (c)(3) would stay with the department. The state share of funding that a charter school student generates would go straight to the charter school. Membership would start on the student's first day and end on the last day. A student who graduates early would count as a member until the expected graduation date for funding purposes.

Section 3 would add "or public charter school" after "LEA" in Section 49-3-316(c). It would also add a new subsection (f). The commissioner of education, with the comptroller, would set up a standard financial accounting and reporting system for all charter schools. It would be designed to allow comparisons across years and agencies and to show the sources and uses of all funds. The commissioner would review charter school fiscal records to make sure spending is properly accounted for and safeguarded. The commissioner could also require charter schools that receive state education funding to follow one or more of the requirements that apply to LEAs in that section, as the commissioner considers appropriate.

Section 4 would replace Section 49-13-112(a). A local board of education would have to give each charter school an amount equal to four items. The first is the local student-generated funds for its member students for the prior year. The second is the average per-pupil state and local funds above those the TISA requires. The third is the per-student state and local funds received for members beyond the prior year's membership. The fourth is all appropriate federal allocations, including IDEA and ESEA funds. The department of education would pay charter schools directly the state student-generated funds for the prior year. Federal funds the LEA receives would go to charter schools through joint agreements for shared services or through sub-grants for an equitable share, following department policies. Each LEA would list in its budget the per-pupil local amount it will pass to charter schools, with its calculations. It would pay the local funds in at least nine equal installments, the same way state funds are paid. It would adjust payments at least in October, February, and June to reflect changes in revenue, membership, or services. Charter schools must spend funds according to their budget, or as their governing body revises it, subject to state and federal law.

Sections 1 and 3 would take effect when the bill becomes law. Sections 2 and 4 would also take effect then for rulemaking. For all other purposes, they would take effect July 1, 2025.
</summary>

claims.claim: The bill would change public charter school funding and financial oversight under Tennessee education funding law.
claims.summary_quote: This bill would change how public charter schools are funded and tracked under Tennessee's education funding law
claims.source_quote:
relative to education
 funding for public charter schools.
claims.rationale: The bill's stated subject and its funding and financial-reporting amendments support this overview.

claims.claim: The text uses TISA to refer to the education funding framework.
claims.summary_quote: which the text refers to as the TISA
claims.source_quote:
in alignment with the TISA
 pursuant to chapter 3, part 1 of this title;
claims.rationale: The bill expressly refers to TISA in its funding provisions.

claims.claim: The state share generated by public charter school students would go directly to their charter school rather than the LEA.
claims.summary_quote: It would send the state share of funding for charter school students directly to the charter school instead of to the local school system (LEA).
claims.source_quote:
The state share of the funding a public charter school student
 generates for an LEA pursuant to this section must not be allocated to the
 LEA, but must be allocated directly to the public charter school.
claims.rationale: Section 2 expressly redirects this state share from the LEA to the public charter school.

claims.claim: LEA means a local school system.
claims.summary_quote: local school system (LEA)
claims.rationale: The supplied text does not define LEA. This is an explanatory expansion, not a demonstrated change to the bill's legal effect.

claims.claim: Section 1 would insert 'or public charter school' into Section 49-3-103(d)(3) after 'Explain how an LEA'.
claims.summary_quote: Section 1 would add "or public charter school" to a provision in Section 49-3-103(d)(3) that begins "Explain how an LEA."
claims.source_quote:
SECTION 1. Tennessee Code Annotated, Section 49-3-103(d)(3), is amended by

adding the language "or public charter school" after the language "Explain how an LEA".
claims.rationale: The insertion, statutory location, and quoted existing language match Section 1.

claims.claim: The existing provision begins with 'Explain how an LEA'.
claims.summary_quote: that begins "Explain how an LEA."
claims.source_quote: adding the language "or public charter school" after the language "Explain how an LEA".
claims.rationale: The bill identifies language after which to insert text, but does not establish that this language begins the provision.

claims.claim: The supplied text does not reproduce the underlying requirement in Section 49-3-103(d)(3).
claims.summary_quote: The text does not show what the provision requires.
claims.source_quote: adding the language "or public charter school" after the language "Explain how an LEA".
claims.rationale: Section 1 supplies only an insertion instruction and a fragment of the existing provision.

claims.claim: Section 2 would replace Section 49-3-105(d).
claims.summary_quote: Section 2 would replace Section 49-3-105(d).
claims.source_quote:
SECTION 2. Tennessee Code Annotated, Section 49-3-105, is amended by deleting

subsection (d) and substituting instead the following:
claims.rationale: This is the amendment expressly directed by Section 2.

claims.claim: The department would administer and allocate student-generated funding to the student's LEA for the duration of membership, subject to exceptions.
claims.summary_quote: Funding a student generates would go through the state department of education to the LEA where the student is a member, for as long as the student is a member.
claims.source_quote:
The funding that a student generates pursuant to this section must be
 administered and allocated by the department to the LEA in which the student is
 a member for the duration of the student's membership in the LEA, except that:
claims.rationale: The summary states the general allocation rule and then separately explains its exceptions.

claims.claim: The general allocation rule has two exceptions.
claims.summary_quote: There are two exceptions.
claims.source_quote:
(A) The funding a student generates pursuant to subdivision
 (c)(3) must not be allocated to the LEA, but must be maintained by the
 department; and

 (B) The state share of the funding a public charter school student
 generates for an LEA pursuant to this section must not be allocated to the
 LEA, but must be allocated directly to the public charter school.
claims.rationale: The replacement subsection lists two exceptions, (A) and (B).

claims.claim: Funding generated under subdivision (c)(3) would remain with the department.
claims.summary_quote: Funding generated under subdivision (c)(3) would stay with the department.
claims.rationale: This accurately describes the first exception.

claims.claim: The state share generated by a public charter school student would be allocated directly to the charter school.
claims.summary_quote: The state share of funding that a charter school student generates would go straight to the charter school.
claims.source_quote:
The state share of the funding a public charter school student
 generates for an LEA pursuant to this section must not be allocated to the
 LEA, but must be allocated directly to the public charter school.
claims.rationale: This accurately describes the second exception.

claims.claim: Ordinary LEA membership would begin on the first day of membership and end on the last day.
claims.summary_quote: Membership would start on the student's first day and end on the last day.
claims.source_quote:
A student's membership in an LEA begins on the first day of the
 student's membership and ends on the last day of the student's membership in
 the LEA
claims.rationale: The summary matches the ordinary membership-duration rule.

claims.claim: Early graduates would remain counted through their expected graduation date for funding purposes.
claims.summary_quote: A student who graduates early would count as a member until the expected graduation date for funding purposes.
claims.source_quote:
except that the membership of a student who graduates early is
 extended to the student's expected graduation date for funding purposes.
claims.rationale: The condition, extension date, and funding-only purpose match the bill.

claims.claim: Section 3 would add 'or public charter school' after 'LEA' in Section 49-3-316(c).
claims.summary_quote: Section 3 would add "or public charter school" after "LEA" in Section 49-3-316(c).
claims.source_quote:
adding the

language "or public charter school" after the language "LEA" wherever it appears in subsection

(c)
claims.rationale: The stated insertion and statutory location are correct.

claims.claim: Section 3 would add a new subsection (f).
claims.summary_quote: It would also add a new subsection (f).
claims.source_quote:
and by adding the following as a new subsection:

 (f)
claims.rationale: The bill expressly adds subsection (f).

claims.claim: The commissioner, working with the comptroller, would establish a standardized financial accounting and reporting system for all public charter schools.
claims.summary_quote: The commissioner of education, with the comptroller, would set up a standard financial accounting and reporting system for all charter schools.
claims.source_quote:
The commissioner, in consultation with the comptroller of the
 treasury, shall develop, revise as necessary, and prescribe a standardized
 system of financial accounting and reporting for all public charter schools
claims.rationale: This captures the mandatory system-development duty and the comptroller's consultative involvement.

claims.claim: The accounting system would facilitate comparisons across years.
claims.summary_quote: It would be designed to allow comparisons across years and agencies
claims.source_quote:
This system must be
 designed to facilitate year-to-year and agency-to-agency comparison
claims.rationale: Year-to-year comparison is an express design requirement.

claims.claim: The accounting system would facilitate comparisons across agencies.
claims.summary_quote: It would be designed to allow comparisons across years and agencies
claims.source_quote:
This system must be
 designed to facilitate year-to-year and agency-to-agency comparison
claims.rationale: Agency-to-agency comparison is also an express design requirement.

claims.claim: The accounting system would show the sources and uses of all funds received by each public charter school.
claims.summary_quote: to show the sources and uses of all funds
claims.source_quote:
adequately indicating the sources and uses of all funds received by each public
 charter school.
claims.rationale: The summary accurately describes the required financial information.

claims.claim: The commissioner would review public charter school fiscal records to ensure expenditures are properly accounted for and safeguarded.
claims.summary_quote: The commissioner would review charter school fiscal records to make sure spending is properly accounted for and safeguarded.
claims.source_quote:
The commissioner shall review the fiscal public school records in
 all public charter schools to the end that the expenditure of funds, whether for
 current operation and maintenance purposes, capital outlay purposes, and other
 school purposes, are properly accounted for and safeguarded.
claims.rationale: The actor, mandatory review, and purpose match the bill.

claims.claim: The commissioner could require public charter schools receiving state education funding to comply with one or more LEA requirements in that section, as deemed appropriate.
claims.summary_quote: The commissioner could also require charter schools that receive state education funding to follow one or more of the requirements that apply to LEAs in that section, as the commissioner considers appropriate.
claims.source_quote:
The commissioner may require public charter schools that receive
 allocations of state education funding pursuant to part 1 of this chapter or
 otherwise to comply with one (1) or more of the requirements established for
 LEAs in this section, as the commissioner deems appropriate or applicable.
claims.rationale: The summary preserves the discretionary authority, eligible schools, and limitation to requirements in the section.

claims.claim: Section 4 would replace Section 49-13-112(a).
claims.summary_quote: Section 4 would replace Section 49-13-112(a).
claims.source_quote:
SECTION 4. Tennessee Code Annotated, Section 49-13-112, is amended by deleting

subsection (a) and substituting instead the following:
claims.rationale: This is the replacement expressly directed by Section 4.

claims.claim: A local board of education would be required to allocate funding to public charter schools.
claims.summary_quote: A local board of education would have to give each charter school an amount equal to four items.
claims.source_quote:
A local board of education shall allocate to the public charter school
 an amount equal to:
claims.rationale: The summary correctly identifies the responsible actor and mandatory allocation duty.

claims.claim: The local board's allocation would consist of four listed components.
claims.summary_quote: an amount equal to four items
claims.source_quote:
(A) The local student-generated funds for member students in the
 public charter school for the prior year in alignment with the TISA
 pursuant to chapter 3, part 1 of this title;

 (B) The average per pupil state and local funds received by the
 district in the current school year above those required by the TISA for
 each member student in the public charter school in the prior year;

 (C) The per student state and local funds received by the LEA for
 member students in the public charter school in the current school year
 beyond the prior year's membership; and

 (D) All appropriate allocations under federal law or regulation,
 including, but not limited to, IDEA and ESEA funds.
claims.rationale: The bill lists four allocation components, (A) through (D).

claims.claim: The first component is local student-generated funding for the charter school's prior-year member students.
claims.summary_quote: The first is the local student-generated funds for its member students for the prior year.
claims.source_quote:
The local student-generated funds for member students in the
 public charter school for the prior year in alignment with the TISA
claims.rationale: The funding type, students, and prior-year basis match component (A).

claims.claim: The second component concerns average per-pupil state and local funding above TISA requirements.
claims.summary_quote: The second is the average per-pupil state and local funds above those the TISA requires.
claims.rationale: This accurately identifies the component; omitted timing and calculation details are coverage issues.

claims.claim: The third component concerns per-student state and local funds for membership beyond the prior year's membership.
claims.summary_quote: The third is the per-student state and local funds received for members beyond the prior year's membership.
claims.rationale: This accurately describes the additional-membership funding component.

claims.claim: The fourth component is all appropriate federal allocations, including IDEA and ESEA funds.
claims.summary_quote: The fourth is all appropriate federal allocations, including IDEA and ESEA funds.
claims.source_quote:
All appropriate allocations under federal law or regulation,
 including, but not limited to, IDEA and ESEA funds.
claims.rationale: The summary matches component (D) without expanding the abbreviations.

claims.claim: The department of education would directly allocate public charter schools their prior-year state student-generated funding.
claims.summary_quote: The department of education would pay charter schools directly the state student-generated funds for the prior year.
claims.source_quote:
The department of education shall allocate directly to the public
charter school an amount equal to the state student-generated funds for member
students in the public charter school for the prior year
claims.rationale: The actor, direct allocation, funding type, and prior-year basis match the bill.

claims.claim: LEA-received federal funds would be distributed to public charter schools through shared-service agreements or equitable-share subgrants.
claims.summary_quote: Federal funds the LEA receives would go to charter schools through joint agreements for shared services or through sub-grants for an equitable share
claims.source_quote:
Federal funds received by the LEA must be disbursed to public
charter schools authorized by the LEA by either joint agreement on shared
services by individual public charter schools or sub-grants to a public charter
school for the public charter school's equitable share of the federal grant based
on eligible students.
claims.rationale: The two distribution mechanisms and equitable-share concept are correct; the summary does not affirmatively extend eligibility to other schools.

claims.claim: Federal allocations would follow department policies.
claims.summary_quote: following department policies
claims.source_quote:
The allocation must be made in accordance with the
policies and procedures developed by the department of education.
claims.rationale: Department policies govern these allocations.

claims.claim: Each LEA would include its per-pupil local pass-through amount for public charter schools in its budget.
claims.summary_quote: Each LEA would list in its budget the per-pupil local amount it will pass to charter schools
claims.source_quote:
Each LEA shall include as part of its budget submitted pursuant to §
49-2-203, the per pupil amount of local money it will pass through to public
charter schools during the upcoming school year
claims.rationale: The budget disclosure requirement is accurately described.

claims.claim: The LEA budget disclosure would include the associated calculations.
claims.summary_quote: with its calculations
claims.source_quote:
including all calculations listed
in this section.
claims.rationale: The bill requires the calculations to accompany the budget amount.

claims.source_quote:
The LEA shall distribute the portion of local
 funds it expects to receive in no fewer than nine (9) equal installments to public

claims.rationale: The minimum number and equal-installment requirement are correct.

claims.claim: Local installments would be distributed in the same manner as state funds.

in the same manner as state funds are distributed pursuant to
 chapter 3 of this title.
claims.rationale: The summary preserves the required correspondence to state-fund distribution.

claims.source_quote:
An LEA shall adjust local payments to public charter
 schools, at a minimum, in October, February, and June
claims.rationale: The mandatory minimum adjustment schedule matches the bill.

claims.claim: Local payment adjustments would reflect changes in revenue, student membership, or student services.
claims.summary_quote: to reflect changes in revenue, membership, or services
claims.source_quote:
based on changes in
 revenue, student membership, or student services.
claims.rationale: The summary accurately identifies the adjustment grounds.

claims.summary_quote: Charter schools must spend funds according to their budget, or as their governing body revises it
claims.source_quote:
All funds received by a public
 charter school must be spent according to the budget submitted or as otherwise
 revised by the public charter school governing body
claims.rationale: The mandatory spending rule and permitted governing-body revisions are accurately stated.

claims.claim: Public charter school spending remains subject to state and federal law.
claims.summary_quote: subject to state and federal law
claims.source_quote:
subject to the requirements
 of state and federal law.
claims.rationale: The summary preserves the express legal constraint on spending.
